info.title: sipsorcery-diags
info.description: Diagnostics and benchmarking CLI for SIP and WebRTC, built on the SIPSorcery library: OPTIONS pings, test calls, registration and load, STUN/TURN/ICE connectivity probes, WHEP/WHIP and echo-test peers, and video pipeline benchmarks. Probe/test tooling (not a general softphone); human and agent friendly with JSON output and meaningful exit codes. For routing streams and the Cloudflare/LiveKit/OpenAI fabric verbs see the SIPSorcery.Cli tool.

commands.description: Send a SIP OPTIONS request and report the response (SIP ping).

commands.name: whep
commands.description: Connect to a WHEP endpoint (full ICE/DTLS/SRTP) and verify media is received.

options.name: --token
options.description: Optional bearer token for the Authorization header. For Broadcast Box this is the stream key.

options.name: --duration
options.description: The number of seconds to receive media for after the connection is established. [default: 5]

options.name: --video
options.description: Where to send the received video: "play" to render in an ffplay window, a file path (H264 is written as Annex B, VP8 in an IVF container), "-" for the bitstream on stdout (the result then moves to stderr), e.g. pipe to "mpv --vo=tct -" for video in the terminal, or "null" to discard it (headless throughput measurement, e.g. with --decode).

options.name: --decode
options.description: Decode the received frames in-process with the SIPSorcery (FFmpeg) video decoder and send raw RGB to the --video sink, instead of passing the encoded bitstream through for the consumer to decode (the default). Requires the FFmpeg shared libraries and a --video sink. [default: False]

options.name: --ffmpeg-path
options.description: Directory containing the FFmpeg shared libraries for --decode. Defaults to the system path.

commands.name: whip
commands.description: Publish a test pattern to a WHIP endpoint using the SIPSorcery stack (full send pipeline: encode, RTP/SRTP, ICE/DTLS).

options.name: --preset
options.description: Resolution preset (360p, 480p, 720p, 1080p, 1440p or 4k). Ignored if --size is given. [default: 720p]

options.name: --size
options.description: Explicit frame size WxH (e.g. 1280x720), overriding --preset.

options.name: --fps
options.description: Target frame rate to publish at (ignored with --max-rate). [default: 30]

options.name: --encoder
options.description: Video encoder: vp8.net (managed Vpx.Net VP8, no native deps) or ffmpeg (SIPSorceryMedia.FFmpeg). [default: vp8.net]

options.name: --codec
options.description: Codec for the ffmpeg encoder: h264 (default), h265, vp8, vp9 or av1. Ignored for vp8.net, which is always VP8.

options.name: --bitrate

options.name: --max-rate
options.description: Send as fast as the encoder and transport allow (ignores --fps) to measure the send pipeline ceiling. Use only against a local receiver, never a remote ingest. [default: False]

commands.name: video-bench
commands.description: Benchmark the video send pipeline (packetisation/encoding) against a target resolution and frame rate.

options.name: --preset
options.description: Resolution preset (360p, 480p, 720p, 1080p, 1440p or 4k); overrides --width/--height when set.

options.name: --width
options.description: The frame width in pixels. [default: 1920]

options.name: --height
options.description: The frame height in pixels. [default: 1080]

options.name: --fps
options.description: The target frame rate to test against. [default: 30]

options.name: --duration
options.description: The number of seconds to run the benchmark for. [default: 5]

options.name: --bitrate
options.description: Target encoded bitrate in bits per second; sets the per-frame size for the packetise stage. 0 (default) derives it from the resolution and frame rate. [default: 0]

options.name: --encoder
options.description: The pipeline stage to test: none (packetise only), ffmpeg (SIPSorceryMedia.FFmpeg in-process encoder), ffmpeg-piped (external ffmpeg process) or vp8.net (managed Vpx.Net codec). The none stage packetises a frame sized from --bitrate/--fps, so it is independent of resolution (width/height are reported for context only). [default: none]

options.name: --codec
options.description: The video codec to encode/packetise as: vp8, vp9, h264, h265 (alias hevc) or av1. The in-process ffmpeg encoder supports all five; vp8.net is VP8 only and ffmpeg-piped supports vp8 and vp9 (IVF) only. [default: vp8]

options.name: --ffmpeg-path
options.description: Directory containing the FFmpeg shared libraries for the --encoder ffmpeg stage. Defaults to the system path.

options.name: --deadline
options.description: libvpx deadline for the ffmpeg stages: realtime, good or best. [default: realtime]

options.name: --cpu-used
options.description: libvpx cpu-used (speed) for the ffmpeg stages. Higher is faster/lower quality (VP8 realtime 0-16). -1 leaves it unset. [default: 5]

options.name: --threads
options.description: Encoder thread count for the ffmpeg stages. 0 lets the encoder decide. [default: 0]

options.name: --av1-encoder
options.description: FFmpeg AV1 encoder for the in-process ffmpeg stage: libsvtav1 (fastest for realtime), libaom-av1, librav1e, or a hardware encoder (av1_nvenc, av1_qsv). Applies to --codec av1 and --all. [default: libsvtav1]

options.name: --av1-preset
options.description: Speed preset for the AV1 encoder, higher is faster (libsvtav1 preset 0-13). -1 uses the encoder's realtime default. [default: -1]

options.name: --all
options.description: Benchmark every video codec (vp8, vp9, h265, av1) with the in-process ffmpeg encoder and report each. Overrides --encoder and --codec. [default: False]

options.name: --json
options.description: Write the result to stdout as a single JSON object instead of human readable text. [default: False]

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Write diagnostic logs, including protocol traces, to stderr. [default: False]
